sentences.text: The present application has been filed with prayer to take appropriate action against the respondent No.4 and other erring officials for behaving in a highhanded manner against the present applicant, stating that the action of the respondent No.4 is against the guidelines laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Arnesh Kumar Vs. State of Bihar & Anr., reported in 2014 (8) SCC 273, and thereby has committed contempt towards the said decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court.

sentences.text: Learned advocate Mr. Ekrama H.Qureshi appearing for the applicant has submitted that the applicant is an advocate by profession and belongs to the family residing at rural remote area of village Kotda, Taluka - Nakhatrana in Kutch
NEUTRAL
CITATION
ORDER DATED: 06/02/2025 undefined District.

It is submitted that the applicant practices in the lower courts of district Kutch and now at Bhuj and the family members of the applicant used to earn their livelihood by running the shops of tyre repair, service station etc., in the village.

3. It is contended by learned advocate Mr. Qureshi that the respondent No.4 made an arrest of the applicant in connection with the F.I.R. bearing FIR No.11205035230193 of 2023 registered with Nakhatrana Police Station, District Kutch under Section 153A of the Indian Penal Code dated 05.03.2023.
It is submitted that the respondent No.4 had not filed any check list before the Magistrate and had made an arrest of the applicant in a highhanded manner and produced him before the Court.

He submitted that it is in gross violation of the conditions and directions laid down in case of Arnesh Kumar (supra).
4.

Learned advocate Mr. Qureshi further stated that respondent No.4 was mandated by the directions issued by the State Government to produce the check list as per Annexure-V, as promulgated and failure to do so, has led to illegal detention, which has therefore, led to gross violation and ultimately, contempt of Court.
5.

Per contra, learned senior advocate Mr. B.B. Naik referring to the provisions of Section 41 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, as referred in Arnesh Kumar (supra), has stressed upon Condition No.4, stating that the check list would be necessary only in case of further detention and that NEUTRAL CITATION C/MCA/2198/2023 ORDER DATED: 06/02/2025 undefined the police could not be obliged to file any check list at the first instance since Section 41 of the Cr.P.C. gives the authority to the police to arrest the person if, he is satisfied with the conditions, as laid down in the said Section.

6. Learned senior advocate Mr. Naik further stated that it is not the case that the respondent No.4 had not produced any check list before the concerned Magistrate while producing the accused and making a prayer for taking the accused in the Court custody, he had filed a check list, which was in a type form and the learned Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate has seen the same and accepted the check list.

It is submitted that the grounds for the arrest has been laid down in the check list and the police had come to its own satisfaction that the arrest of the applicant would be necessary, as that would create tension between the two communities since he had some writing placed in the Whatsapp status and therefore, that would have lead to promoting enmity between two groups and ultimately, breach of public order.
7. Heard learned advocates appearing for both the sides and perused the documents on record.

The record suggests that while producing the accused in the Court custody, the learned Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate had accepted the custody of the applicant and the check list, which was seen and accepted by the learned Judge.

However, it requires to be noted that the State Government vide its notification with the subject of Guidelines for the arrest of accused persons in connection with the investigation in criminal cases under Section 498A and as per the direction of the Hon'ble Apex Aasif Salemamad Kumbhar vs State Of Gujarat on 6 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/160554465/
2

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: NEUTRAL CITATION C/MCA/2198/2023 ORDER DATED: 06/02/2025 undefined Court, has formulated a check list to be filled in cases other than under Section 498A and Section 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act.

The check list, which is to be noted at Annexure-V with the bracketed information that such check list has to be enclosed along with the application while seeking police remand or remanding of the accused to judicial custody, in cases other than section, as noted.

8. The present respondent No.4, as it appears from the record that though had followed according to the guideline, as issued by the State Government but the Form, which was mandated to be filled as per Annexure-V, had not been produced before the concerned Judge.

The check list, which has been referred to was seen and accepted by the Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate in the type copy, while the respondent No.4 was required to fill in the necessary information, as was mandated in the Form of Annexure-V.
It appears that the said procedure has not been followed.

However, we are of the opinion that such act of the respondent No.4 would not be an illegality but is an irregularity since,
the procedure though was followed, as mandated by the State and as per the direction in Arnesh Kumar (supra), but the check list was not in the prescribed form.

9. Learned senior advocate Mr. Naik has also referred to the affidavit dated 13.03.2024 of the respondent No.4, wherein the respondent No.4 has tendered unconditional apology in following terms:
NEUTRAL CITATION C/MCA/2198/2023 ORDER DATED: 06/02/2025 undefined "2. I say and submit that the Respondents herein have not willfully disobeyed an Order passed or direction issued by the Hon'ble Apex Court in case of Arnesh Kumar Vs. State of Bihar and Others and the Deponent has the highest esteem and respect to all the Hon'ble Courts and respect the Orders passed and the directions issued by the Hon'ble Courts.

entities.text: Arnesh Kumar Vs. State of Bihar and Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: However, if this Hon'ble Court is of the opinion that the Deponent has not properly complied with the Order issued by this Hon'ble Court, the deponent hereby tenders unconditional apology for the same.
11. I tender my sincere and unconditional apology for the inconvenience caused to the Hon'ble Court once again.

The deponent thus humbly solicits for apologies as there was a delay in complying with the order of this Hon'ble Single Judge and there was no action or inaction on the Deponent's part which may amount to will-full disobedience of the order of this Hon'ble Court and hence the contempt proceedings be set back in the interest of justice."

10. We are of the opinion that the respondent No.4 had not perceived the directions, as laid down in Arnesh Kumar (supra) in its right sense and has not followed the direction, as given by the State Government to fill in the details as per the check list.

However, the concerned Court before whom the applicant was produced, had accepted the check list, as was given by the respondent No.4, the same was required to be filed in the format since, it is for the details which were required to be perceived by the concerned Judge for considering the satisfaction of the genuineness which had been approached by the respondent No.4 for making arrest and for further remand or for sending the applicant in judicial custody.

sentences.text:
The respondent No.4 has failed to proceed as per the direction of Arnesh Kumar (supra), but since the check list had been seen and accepted by the Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate and the cause, which was given for the NEUTRAL CITATION C/MCA/2198/2023 ORDER DATED:
06/02/2025 undefined investigation and the arrest was found to be genuine, this Court considers that this is a mere irregularity and not an illegality.

Thus, respondent No.4 is directed that henceforth he is to be very careful while delivering his duties to follow the conditions and directions,
as laid down in the case of Arnesh Kumar (supra) and the direction of the State Government while filling up the check list.
12. In view of the above observations and directions, the present application stands disposed of.
